12.11.2.en: No one can deny that some enjoy wisdom, which they receive with the experience of the years and length of days. "How beautiful is wisdom in the aged, and understanding and counsel to men of honour" (Sir 25:7).

12.11.3.en: They may have wisdom, perception and understanding of matters, yet they are unable to carry out their wisdom, whereas God is all-wise and all-powerful.

12.11.4.en: Perhaps Job wanted to declare to them that they had been hasty in judging him because they saw him falling into many trials. It would have been fitting for them to wait for a period of time so that, with true wisdom, they might see what lies behind the trials.

12.11.5.en: St. John Chrysostom says in the person of Job: [Do we, because we know this much, think that we know everything? I know that the wicked are punished, but you see that, in spite of my righteousness, I too am punished. Besides this, does the matter require time for you to understand something that has so many similar examples? Do you not see how the Holy Bible presents depth of experience? What the ancients acquired by experience of events in detail, you who are younger than they offer many thanks to the one who recounts the events. Many sorrows came upon them, and from many sides; and you also, if you search the Holy Scriptures with great care, will see many of them (who entered into afflictions). This is the reason for the saying of one: "Be willing to listen to a good discourse," and in another place he says: [Despise not the discourse of the ancients... for of them thou shalt learn understanding] (Sir 6:35; 8:8-9). You do not need time; for if God Himself wishes to give it to you, you are in no need of time.]

12.11.6.en: * [With the ancient is wisdom; and in length of days understanding] [12]. This is because we acquire wisdom by study, and learning is planted in the mind by the lessons of men. With God it is otherwise, for He Himself is Wisdom in His person, and He is the One who teaches the lessons of wisdom.

12.11.7.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem * These sayings establish the roots of wisdom, for as life continues wisdom is strengthened, through the practice of works. But since there are many to whom length of life has been given, and wisdom has not been given, it appears fitting that He who has the decision to give these gifts says: [With him is wisdom and strength, he hath counsel and understanding].

12.11.9.en: With him is wisdom and strength,

12.12.1.en: God, who alone is all-wise, perceives all things and is able to accomplish His will, for He is also all-powerful. There is no comparison between the wisdom of the aged and the wisdom of God.

12.12.2.en: "Give me wisdom, that sitteth by thy throne; and reject me not from among thy children" (Wis 9:4).

12.12.3.en: "For though a man be never so perfect among the children of men, yet if thy wisdom be not with him, he shall be nothing regarded" (Wis 9:6).

12.12.4.en: "Thy wisdom was with thee, which knoweth thy works, and was present when thou madest the world, and knew what was acceptable in thy sight, and right in thy commandments" (Wis 9:9).

12.12.5.en: "The word of God most high is the fountain of wisdom; and her ways are everlasting commandments" (Sir 1:5).

12.12.6.en: * [With him is wisdom and strength, he hath counsel and understanding] [13]. Job did not speak entirely without offering testimony, nor without a defense (of his opinion); rather, he supports his words with the testimony of the creatures, for the beauty of the visible elements proclaims the wisdom of God and His great power.

12.12.7.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem * The work of the Father, which pervades all existence, is glorified and greatly magnified when every man advances and reaches the highest stature of growth through fellowship with Christ, "Wisdom," "Knowledge" and "Holiness."

12.12.8.en: The same thing is fulfilled when a man is sanctified and purified and reaches the highest degrees of perfection through fellowship with the Holy Spirit, and so becomes more worthy to receive the grace of wisdom and knowledge, until every stain of defilement and ignorance is removed from him, and he reaches this progress in perfection and purity. In this way the life he has received from God is worthy of God, who intends it to be pure and perfect. Then the creature becomes worthy of this (holy) life (and is made in the likeness of the Creator); for in this way, which the Creator wills for him, man receives from Him the power to exist eternally...

12.12.9.en: * God cares for the soul [that is, the seat of the faculties, feelings and sensations] in every man, that he may be rational and receive knowledge, and that his intelligence may work in a fitting manner in the midst of the life of the body, so that his feelings and perceptions (Heb 5:14) become sound.

12.12.10.en: Origen Behold, he breaketh down, and it cannot be built again;

12.13.0.en: he shutteth up a man, and there can be no opening [14].

12.13.1.en: He who possesses God enjoys His wisdom and power working in him; but he who resists the wisdom of God with his human wisdom will meet with nothing but folly. His life is broken down by divine permission, and there is no one who can build it up. Job takes us back to the age of the building of the tower of Babel, where man relied on his own wisdom and power and thought that he was able to resist God. They thought they could build a tower in heaven, but they failed and their energy was scattered. And behold the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah bears witness to the failure of resisting God.

12.13.2.en: God shuts up by permitting sickness or calamity, or He allows a man to die, so that he enters the grave and does not come out of it. When He shuts up the wicked in hell, who can bring them up from there?

12.13.3.en: When a man insists on shutting up his heart upon the practice of a sin and does not open it to receive God's grace and support, the sin remains a prisoner in his heart; it reigns over him and leads him while it is in the prison of the closed heart. So it happened with Pharaoh, who refused in his heart to listen to the voice of God through the plagues, and while he made promises with his deceitful mouth, he harbored in his heart violence and resistance to the work of God. Therefore it was said: "But I will harden Pharaoh's heart" (Ex 7:3), by leaving him a prisoner of his evil and violence.

12.13.4.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) gives us another example of one whose heart became closed, namely Esau. He closed his heart by his own will, through his evil and carelessness, until he sold his birthright for a meal of lentils, saying: [Behold, I am at the point to die: and what profit shall this birthright do to me?] (Gen 25:32). Esau despised the birthright, and did not repent of this or of his evils, so his heart was shut up in its evil. His father wanted to open this door to give him the blessing before he died (Gen 27:4), but the Lord rejected this son because he did not repent, and the father gave the blessing to the younger son against his will. Esau cried out with a great cry that did not come from a humble, contrite soul, so his repentance became as nothing, unable to draw God's grace to open his heart.

12.13.5.en: * Almighty God breaks down the heart of man when He abandons it, and builds it up when He fills it; for He does not break down the soul of man by entering into war, but by withdrawing from it. When the heart is left to itself, it goes to nothing, indeed to its own destruction. Therefore, when it happens that the heart of the hearer is not filled with the grace of Almighty God, because of his sins, the preacher offers his counsels to him from outside in vain. Every mouth that speaks then is as if it were mute, unless God utters a voice in the heart from within, He who inspires the words that are presented to the ear. So the prophet says: "Except the LORD build the house, they labour in vain that build it" (Ps 127:1). Solomon says: [Consider the work of God: for who can make that straight, which he hath made crooked?] (Eccl 7:13)...

12.13.6.en: Cain was able to enjoy counsels issuing from the voice of God, and yet he could not change. Because of the sin of his evil heart within, God left him, although He addressed words to him from outside to bear witness against him.

12.13.7.en: Well did he add: "He shutteth up a man, and there can be no opening" [14]. For every man who practices wrong in all his ways, what does he do but make of himself a prison for his conscience? The sense of guilt in the soul may press upon him even if no one accuses him from outside. And if he is left in the blindness of his evil heart by God's judgment, he is like one who has shut himself in, so that he finds no place to flee, and does not deserve to find such a place. For it often happens that persons long to leave their evil habits, but because they are weighed down to the earth by their burden, they shut up the evil habit in the prison and cannot themselves come out of themselves.

12.13.9.en: * We learn from this (Ps 127:1) that it is not because God is the One who builds that a man sits idle, as though God would build the house for him. Rather, he works and takes care as far as his human abilities allow, but God removes all obstacles and completes the work. Thus man is called to work as much as he can, in earnestness, but it is God who crowns the work with success. Therefore it is fitting for man, rightly and in godliness, to leave the completion of his work to God, and not to another human being. On this basis Paul planted and Apollos watered, but God gave the increase, for neither is he that planteth anything, neither he that watereth, but God that giveth the increase (1 Cor 3:6-7). In the same way we can say that this depends not on the will of man or his striving, but on the mercies of God.

12.13.10.en: Origen * We cannot run in the way of God unless we are carried on the wings of the Spirit.

12.13.11.en: * It is with God's help that we do the good that we practice.

12.13.12.en: * No one is stronger than he who enjoys heavenly help, just as no one is weaker than he who is deprived of it.

12.13.13.en: * Let us be stronger than all, imitating Paul, Peter, James and John; for if God's help is absent from us, we cannot resist the most trifling temptation.

12.13.14.en: * We fear nothing, for in order to defeat Satan we must know that our skill will profit nothing, and that everything is from the grace of God.

12.13.15.en: * Those who are punished, it is on account of justice; but those who are crowned, it is on account of grace. Even if they had practiced a thousand good works, they enjoy heaven and the Kingdom in return for these small works only by the freedom of grace, and so they are lifted up to what cannot be measured.

12.13.16.en: St. John Chrysostom Behold, he withholdeth the waters, and they dry up:

12.14.0.en: also he sendeth them out, and they overturn the earth [15].

12.14.1.en: The rains are in the hand of God; if He withholds them, the earth dries up and its fruits perish (Job 4:7). And if He allows them in abundance, the flood of sweeping rain destroys the crops of the earth and buildings collapse. Perhaps he refers here to the flood of Noah, when the earth was drowned.

12.14.2.en: * If He shuts heaven, who can open it? And if He opens the windows of the flood, who can shut them? Who can increase the rain or hold it back from falling in sufficient measure, except the One who governs the universe by His measure and His balances?

12.14.3.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus * If you understand "the waters" as the knowledge of preaching, as it is written: "The words of a man's mouth are as deep waters, and the wellspring of wisdom as a flowing brook" (Prov 18:4), then when the waters are withheld everything becomes dry. This means that when the knowledge of the preacher is withheld, the hearts of those who ought to have been refreshed with the hope of eternity dry up. They may remain in the barrenness of hopelessness, through their love of temporal things...

12.14.4.en: And if the expression "the waters" refers to the gift of the Holy Spirit, as the voice of Truth said in the Gospel: "He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water," adding: "This spake he of the Spirit, which they that believe on him should receive" (Jn 7:38-39)... then when the Holy Spirit is withheld from the mind of the hearer, the sense at once becomes dry, which through hope seemed green in the hearer.

12.14.6.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) says: [When Paul was on his way to Damascus, armed with letters against Christ, he was watered on his journey by the grace of the Holy Spirit, and was immediately changed from his intention to shed blood; and afterward he received for Christ's sake the blows that on his journey he had wished to pour out upon the Christians. He who before, walking according to the flesh, strove to deliver the saints of the Lord to death, came to rejoice to offer the sacrifice of his body for the life of the saints. He who was cold, aiming at cruelty, was turned into the warmth of tenderness; and he who was formerly a blasphemer and persecutor became a humble preacher full of tenderness. He who counted the slaughter of Christ in His disciples a great gain, [now holds fast to Christ to be his life, counting death gain] (Phil 1:21). So [he sendeth out the waters, and they overturn the earth] [15], in the mind of Paul, at the moment in which he received the grace of the Holy Spirit, which changed the steadfastness of his obstinacy and cruelty.]

12.14.7.en: * The first waters brought forth life; let no one marvel if the waters in Baptism can also give life.

12.14.8.en: * The Spirit of God was borne upon the waters, He who renews the creation of the one who is baptized. The Holy One was borne upon the holy waters, or rather upon the waters that receive holiness from Him. Thus the waters were sanctified by the Spirit and received the possibility of sanctifying. This is the reason why, since the waters were the primary element (of creation), they obtained the mystery of sanctification through the invocation of God.

12.14.9.en: Tertullian * The new creation is accomplished by water and the Spirit, as in the creation of the world, when the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.

12.14.10.en: St. Clement of Alexandria With him is strength and wisdom:

12.15.0.en: the deceived and the deceiver are his [16].

12.15.1.en: He is the One who has power and strength, and He is the source of wisdom and understanding. He cares for all men, even the simple whom others lead astray, and the crafty who lead their brothers astray. He uses all things to accomplish His divine plan, for both the deceiver and the deceived are under His hands. He is glorified in all, although He does not accept error, craftiness and cunning. In the end the believers sing: "Alleluia: for the Lord God omnipotent reigneth" (Rev 19:6).

12.15.2.en: * If anyone has power and authority, or has acquired understanding and prudence, this is from God; he receives them from Him, who gives generously to those who wish to receive. And it is clear that He takes them back from whom He wishes. Among many, there is an example that teaches you this, namely Nebuchadnezzar, whose power was great, of whom Daniel said: "It is thou, O king, that art grown and become strong: for thy greatness is grown, and reacheth unto heaven, and thy dominion to the end of the earth" (Dan 4:22). Nevertheless, since he exalted himself in pride on every occasion, he lost not only his authority and kingdom, but also knowledge and understanding, [and was driven from men, and did eat grass as oxen] (Dan 4:33). He came to think like a beast, and not as men think. Why did this happen to him? Daniel explained this very clearly: "Seven times shall pass over thee, till thou know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will" (Dan 4:25). And when (Nebuchadnezzar) knew this, he recovered his spirit, and at the same time his kingship, when he offered praise and glory to God (Dan 4:34-37).

12.16.0.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem He leadeth counsellors away spoiled, and maketh the judges fools [17].

12.16.1.en: Not only individuals are under His authority, but even the movements of nations and peoples do not escape the hands of the Ruler of all.

12.16.2.en: He often allows fools who think themselves wise counsellors to fall into captivity like spoils of war, robbed of their dignity, wealth and freedom; they are robbed not only of their wisdom but sometimes, as it were, of their humanity.

12.16.3.en: Even judges who are known for their counsel and the loftiness of their thoughts sometimes become fools, just as God made foolish the counsel of Ahithophel, who became true to his name, for it means "brother of folly or stupidity." As it was said by Isaiah: "The princes of Zoan are become fools; the princes of Noph are deceived; and they that are the chiefs of her tribes have led Egypt astray" (Isa 19:13).

12.16.4.en: Often the aged, who have long experience and wisdom, lose their ability to understand; the very factor of time that led them to wisdom is the one that causes the weakness of old age, and returns them to a state resembling childhood, like one who has neither experience nor understanding.

12.16.5.en: * [He leadeth counsellors away to a foolish end] [17], that is, when they do good without a good purpose, but seek temporal reward. For if the only Son of God the Father, the Most High, became man to preach eternal truths, and for this reason was called [the Angel of Great Counsel] (Isa 9:6), then we rightly interpret "the counsellors" as the preachers who supply their hearers with the counsel of life. But when any preacher proclaims eternal truths in order to gain temporal profits, he surely [goes to a foolish end], since he aims to attain that by his wearisome labors, from which an upright mind ought to flee.

12.16.7.en: * The thought of "vainglory" is the most wicked of all kinds of thoughts.

12.16.8.en: This thought comes to those who walk in the life of righteousness, and the man begins to glorify his own striving and to gather for himself the praise of others. He imagines the demons' terror of him, his healing of women, the crowds thronging around him touching the hem of his garment, and finally he foresees his own consecration to the priesthood, and that people will come to him to make him a priest, and when he refuses the priesthood they bind him and lead him against his will.

12.16.9.en: After Satan has kindled in him these false hopes, he withdraws, leaving the field to other battles brought by the demon of pride or the demon of murmuring, who comes at once and presents him with thoughts contrary to these hopes, so that at times he surrenders to the thoughts of the demon of fornication, he who a few moments before saw himself as a saint and a venerable priest!

12.16.10.en: As for the "demon of pride," he is the cause of the soul's most grievous fall. He advises the soul not to look to God as its helper, but to attribute to itself everything that is good. Then it begins to swell up before the brethren and reckons them ignorant, because they do not know its lofty rank.

12.16.11.en: Pride is followed by anger and murmuring. And the last evil is followed by the man's losing his senses, by fury, and by seeing many demons in the air.

12.16.12.en: *It is hard for you to escape the thought of vainglory, because everything you do to drive it away can become a helping factor in creating a new motive toward vainglory. Moreover, the demons do not always resist every sound thought, but sometimes they encourage in us some sound thoughts in the hope that afterward they can deceive us.

12.17.0.en: St. Evagrius He looseth the bond of kings, and girdeth their loins with a girdle [18].

12.17.1.en: God sometimes permits those in authority, such as kings, to be brought down from their positions and stripped of all honor. He looses their belts, so the sword falls from their side and the crowns from their heads. Perhaps he refers here to their descent to become slaves, since slaves did not gird their loins.

12.18.0.en: He leadeth priests away spoiled, and overthroweth the mighty [19].

12.18.1.en: Having spoken of the classes of the wise, such as counsellors and judges, of the classes of those with experience, such as the aged, and of the classes of those with authority, such as kings, he now speaks of those who think themselves righteous, namely the class of priests. These, in their hypocrisy, sometimes think that they cannot be touched because they are servants of God and work on behalf of His people. But God has no partiality; even His priests He allows to be taken captive, and they lose their dignity, their authority and the wealth in which they took pride.

12.18.2.en: Finally he refers to the class of the mighty: the strong man quickly becomes weak. How many men of mighty strength have fallen into the trap of weak men, and how many strong armies have been defeated before armies weaker than they. So it is not fitting for anyone to rely on his temporal strength, nor on his own wisdom and mere human understanding, nor his authority, nor his social or religious position.

12.18.3.en: * [He leadeth priests away to shame, and overthroweth the mighty] [19]. The great glory of the priest is the righteousness of those subject to him. The excellent preacher rightly says to his disciples: "For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of rejoicing? Are not even ye in the presence of our Lord Jesus Christ at his coming?" (1 Thess 2:19). But priests neglect the lives of those entrusted to them, and do not bear fruit as they advance before the Lord. Thus they come into shame, finding no glory before the strict Judge, those who do not seek Him in the lives of those they serve through their urgency in preaching.

12.18.4.en: Well did he say: "and overthroweth the mighty." By a just judgment He leaves the hearts of those who rule, if they do not look to the inward reward, and they are cast out, where they deceive themselves by rejoicing in temporal glory instead of eternal.

12.18.6.en: *The fault is not in authority in itself, but in vain covetousness. Accordingly, the establishment of authority comes from God, and whoever exercises it is an ambassador of God, being God's minister for good (Rom 13:3-4). The act in itself is not sin, but the fault lies in the one who carries it out... We must distinguish between the good use of authority and the bad use.

12.19.0.en: St. Ambrose He removeth away the speech of the trusted, and taketh away the understanding of the aged [20].

12.19.1.en: When those who excel in eloquence, oratory and philosophies take pride in their linguistic creativity or the attractiveness of their personalities, they sometimes stand as mutes, with not a word in their mouth, because they insulted Him who gave them the mind and granted them the gift of speech and created their mouths.

12.19.2.en: * [He changeth the lips of the trusted, and taketh away the teachings of the aged] [20]. When the priest does not practice the good that he proclaims, the very work of his lips is taken from him, so that he does not dare to utter what he does not practice. It was said by the prophet: "But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?" (Ps 50:16). Likewise he asks Him: "And take not the word of truth utterly out of my mouth" (Ps 119:43). For it appears that Almighty God gives the word of truth to those who practice it, and takes it away from those who do not practice it...

12.19.3.en: The Truth says in the Gospel: "For out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh. A good man out of the good treasure of the heart bringeth forth good things: and an evil man out of the evil treasure bringeth forth evil things" (Mt 12:34-35)... Likewise John says: "They are of the world: therefore speak they of the world" (1 Jn 4:5). Well was it said: [He who changeth the lips of the trusted, and taketh away the teachings of the aged].

12.19.5.en: * "A bishop then must be blameless" (d)... All the virtues are contained in this phrase, and so it seems as if the Apostle demands an impossible perfection. For if any sin or any idle word deserves blame, who in this world is without sin and without blame? And yet he who is chosen as shepherd of the Church must be distinguished from the others, who in truth are a flock of (rational) sheep.

12.19.6.en: If the eloquent define the orator as [a good man skilled in speaking], since he must be without fault in his conduct as in his lips (his oratory) in order to be worthy of praise, because the teacher whose words are not supported by his deeds loses all influence over his hearers.

12.19.7.en: St. Jerome * "Blameless"... This phrase contains all the virtues, so that if a man knows of some sin in himself, it is not good for him to covet an office for which he is not qualified; rather he needs a guide, and not to act as a guide. For he who plays a leading role must be more radiant than any shining star. His life must be without fault, and all look to him and imitate his conduct.

12.19.8.en: St. John Chrysostom Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that this phrase applies to the Jews, whose lips uttered the truth before the Incarnation of the Word; they believed that He was coming, and proclaimed His coming, but their lips changed after His coming, and they denied Him. He became present in their midst, He whose coming they had proclaimed beforehand. But they took away the teachings of their fathers, since they did not walk according to what their fathers prophesied to them about Him.

12.20.0.en: He poureth contempt upon princes, and weakeneth the strength of the mighty [21].

12.20.1.en: When the honorable insult their Creator, they reap contempt for themselves. "He poureth contempt upon princes, and causeth them to wander in the wilderness, where there is no way" (Ps 107:40).

12.20.2.en: * [He poureth contempt upon princes, and raiseth up the persecuted] [21]. The Jewish people continued in the commandment of the Law, while the whole Gentile world knew nothing of the commandment of God; the former were called honorable through faith, while the others fell into the passion of unbelief. But when Judaism denied the mystery of the Incarnation of our Lord, and the Gentile world believed in Him, the honorable fell into contempt, and those who had descended into the sin of unbelief were raised up and received the freedom of the true faith. Jeremiah, seeing this long before it happened, said: "The Lord was as an enemy: he hath swallowed up Israel, he hath swallowed up all his palaces: he hath destroyed his strong holds" (Lam 2:5).

12.20.4.en: * When God rejected Israel, grace flowed to the Gentiles; the calling of the Gentiles began with the fall of Israel, and they receive by the grace of God Jesus Christ, whom the prophets had foretold.

12.20.5.en: * We Christians say that the Jews, though they previously enjoyed God's favor, being loved by Him more than others, yet this divine dispensation and grace have been transferred to us, when Jesus transferred the authority that worked among the Jews to the believers from the Gentiles.

12.21.0.en: Origen He discovereth deep things out of darkness, and bringeth out to light the shadow of death [22].

12.21.1.en: When the first man fell into disobedience, death came to accompany his mind like a shadow, indeed more closely attached than a shadow. Nothing terrifies him like death, so that the Apostle Paul called it "the last enemy," or the most violent enemy that confronts man. But the death of the Lord Christ on the Cross destroyed the power of death in its own lair. By death He trampled death, and granted us the power of eternal life and resurrection.

12.21.2.en: The Lord Christ removed the expression "death" from the dictionary of our thought, and in its place came the expression "the shadow of death," or "sleep," or "departure." We sing, saying: "There is no death for Your servants, but a departure." And we chant with the Apostle Paul, saying: "O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory?" (1 Cor 15:55).

12.21.3.en: The Lord exposed death, so that it became a shadow without substance in the lives of those who believe in Him. He shone with His light upon the tombs, and the weakness of the shadow of death was exposed.

12.21.4.en: The Lord lifted the covering from the darkness, and we realized that we have no place in the kingdom of darkness, since the Sun of Righteousness has shone upon us.

12.21.5.en: God exposes the plots that are devised in darkness, and the evil that is committed in secret. When the king of Aram thought that there was a traitor among his men, one of his servants said to him: "Elisha, the prophet that is in Israel, telleth the king of Israel the words that thou speakest in thy bedchamber" (2 Kgs 6:12).

12.21.6.en: * [He discovereth deep things out of darkness] [22]. What are the deep things? The hidden matters, the thoughts that do not appear in the brightness of the day. This is the reason that Job speaks of darkness. For Christ Himself uses the same words to affirm and confirm the words of Job when He says to the Apostles: "For there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; and hid, that shall not be known" (Mt 10:26). Remember the words He added: "What I tell you in darkness, that speak ye in light: and what ye hear in the ear, that preach ye upon the housetops" (Mt 10:27).

12.21.7.en: "And bringeth out to light the shadow of death" [22]. The shadow of death is sin, in the same way that the shadow reveals the body that casts the shadow; so sin means [The sting of death is sin] (1 Cor 15:56), and it is its distinguishing characteristic.

12.21.8.en: In any case, this shadow of death makes known its mystery (Rom 16:25; Col 1:26) to mankind, and makes known its righteousness (Ps 98:2; Rom 1:17); in the same manner it uncovers sin (Eph 4:22) and does not allow it to be hidden. And since we know its ugliness and that it corrupts the soul, let us all flee from it! This is the reason that Christ said of the Jewish people: "If I had not come and spoken unto them, they had not had sin" (Jn 15:22), in other words, they would not have known the power of sin. But He adds: "but now they have no cloke for their sin," because they knew its defilement, its evil smell and its wickedness when compared with the righteousness and beauty that had not been known before.

12.21.9.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem Pope Gregory (the Great) sees in the shadow of death a reference to the severity of the Law, which stressed that everyone who sins deserves the death of the body; but when the Savior came He removed the death of the body as a penalty for the one who commits sin, and directed our eyes to the seriousness of the working of sin on our souls.

12.21.10.en: He increaseth the nations, and destroyeth them:

12.22.0.en: he enlargeth the nations, and straiteneth them again (scattereth them) [23].

12.22.1.en: God is the Ruler of all history; He sometimes allows some to grow and have authority to achieve a certain aim for the discipline of His people, as happened with Babylon, which was a small state that soon defeated great Assyria and took its place, and carried Judah into captivity; and when Babylon exalted itself against God, in moments it collapsed and was taken by Persia and Media. She who was the head became the tail, and even vanished.

12.22.2.en: * [He maketh the nations to wander and destroyeth them; he scattereth them and then bringeth them in] [23]... It is not He who leads the nations away, but He allows them to wander; they go of themselves to destruction through their evils, since they do not wish to return to faith in Him. As for the scattered nations, Job would say to the Lord: "Scatter them," while He wishes to lead those who desire to run toward the light (Isa 60:3) to enjoy the preaching. He will not transgress justice, but acts as is fitting with each one, whether in faith or in unbelief. Therefore, when Simeon took the Lord, the Child, in his arms, he said: "This child is set for the fall and rising again of many" (Lk 2:34).

12.23.0.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem He taketh away the heart of the chief of the people of the earth, and causeth them to wander in a wilderness where there is no way [24].

12.23.1.en: Who are the chiefs of the earth who lose their understanding, if not the sons of Abraham according to the flesh, who withdrew from their spiritual sonship to him by denying the Savior of the world, and rejecting Him whose day their father Abraham rejoiced to see, many generations before His coming?

12.23.2.en: Their denial turned their lives into a barren wilderness, where their hearts are not watered by the waters of the Holy Spirit, who turns the wildernesses into a divine paradise!

12.23.3.en: * [He changeth the hearts of the chiefs of the people of the earth] [24]. By the words "people of the earth" a man needs to understand the Jewish people, because they clung to earthly things. Paul also spoke of those who [set their minds on earthly things]. Their chiefs are the priests, the scribes and the Pharisees. By the changing of their hearts he means that He turns them.

12.23.4.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem * For since there remained for them no altar, no temple and no priest, and therefore they had no sacrificial offerings, they felt that their sin remained in them, and that there was no way for them to obtain forgiveness.

12.23.5.en: Origen * Behold, Samaritans and Galileans have believed in Christ, to the shame and confusion of the Jews; and the Samaritans were found better than the Galileans, because those Samaritans received Him from the word of the woman, while the Galileans received Him because of His miracles. The Evangelist reminds the hearer of the miracle (the turning of water into wine at Cana of Galilee) to raise the praise of the Samaritans, for the men of Cana received Him because of the miracle that was done in Jerusalem, and this was not the case with the Samaritans, who received Him on account of His teaching alone.

12.24.0.en: St. John Chrysostom They grope in the dark without light, and he maketh them to stagger like a drunken man [25].

12.24.1.en: Those who were leaders of great peoples, with their military power and their fearful authority, soon lost everything and came into humiliation and weakness. As the Psalmist says: "The stouthearted are spoiled... none of the men of might have found their hands" (Ps 76:5). They became like those who are lost "in a wilderness where there is no way" [24]. They feel for the way in the darkness and stagger like drunkards, without consciousness, without thought, and without strength.

12.24.2.en: Thus Job speaks of God, the Ruler of all, in the grasp of whose hand is all history, turning events to the account of His Kingdom. No power can resist Him!

12.24.3.en: * Why? Because they [loved darkness rather than light] (Jn 3:19), in such a way that the Lord Himself became their accuser. Why did they love darkness rather than light? Because their deeds are evil. For it is inevitable that those who practice evils [stagger like a drunken man]. For like drunkards they are befuddled, unable to distinguish between one thing and another, or between evil and good.

12.24.4.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem * O company of the Jews, when you come to Jerusalem and find that it has been laid waste and turned to dust and ashes, do not weep like children (1 Cor 4). Do not grieve, but seek for yourselves a city in heaven instead of the one you seek here on earth. Lift up your eyes, and you will find on high the Jerusalem which is free, which is the mother of us all (Gal 4:26).

12.24.5.en: Do not grieve over the absence of the temple here, nor despair over your lack of a priest. For in heaven you will find an altar and priests of the good things to come, after the order of Melchizedek, in their procession before God (Heb 5:10). For the love and mercy of the Lord willed to remove from you the earthly inheritance, so that you might seek the heavenly.

12.24.7.en: You have granted me wisdom to glorify You, not to examine Your works!

12.24.8.en: * Glory to You, O Giver of mind, thought, heart and all human faculties!

12.24.9.en: It is not for me to exalt myself over Your creation, my brothers in humanity.

12.24.10.en: You are wonderful in Your wisdom, distributing all gifts to mankind.

12.24.11.en: Grant me a holy mind, and a heart that bears You within it.

12.24.12.en: Sanctify my whole being, sanctify my thought and my heart.

12.24.13.en: Lift up my thought, O Lord, by Your Spirit, that I may honor every colleague of mine.

12.24.14.en: Fill my heart, that it may open wide with love for every human being.

12.24.15.en: * My God, how my soul is embittered by the mockery of my loved ones!

12.24.16.en: I have become to them a byword and a laughingstock!

12.24.17.en: But I look to You, and I see You wounded in the house of Your loved ones!

12.24.18.en: My soul rejoices and glorifies You, for You have allowed me to share in Your sufferings!

12.24.19.en: I have truly understood that in wisdom You allowed my loved ones to wound me!

12.24.20.en: I accept these wounds as a crown of glory that I do not deserve.

12.24.21.en: In the midst of the bitterness of my soul I feel for Your comforting hand.

12.24.22.en: I understand that every mockery that befalls me is by Your permission.

12.24.23.en: In Your wondrous love You wanted me to share with You in Your reproaches!

12.24.24.en: I see that darkness cannot bear the light.

12.24.25.en: And corruption thinks that it is able to destroy incorruption.

12.24.26.en: And the fallen devil thinks that he has authority!

12.24.27.en: Glory to You, who turn my sufferings into a joyful hymn, so that I see the earnest of heaven revealed in my depths.

12.24.28.en: Let me realize, O Lord, that Your plan for me is surpassing.

12.24.29.en: Then I will rejoice in my brothers' mockery of me.

12.24.30.en: While they mock me, the heavenly ones see me in surpassing glory!

12.24.31.en: Surely these temporary moments will soon pass, and I will pass with You into the bosom of Your Father, and enjoy fellowship in heavenly glory!

12.24.32.en: The winter with its snow will pass, and the spring of eternity will come with its splendor.

12.24.33.en: * My God, You have granted mankind wisdom and understanding to glorify You.

12.24.34.en: Behold, even creation bears witness to Your wisdom, Your love and Your care!

12.24.35.en: Creation, visible and hidden, glorifies You!

12.24.36.en: All bear witness to Your incomprehensible wisdom.

12.24.37.en: * Grant me to worship at Your feet.

12.24.38.en: With all my heart I praise You for what I know of You, or what I do not yet know.

12.24.39.en: Truly, I stand perplexed before Your wisdom; I see wicked men and robbers who think themselves kings and gods.

12.24.40.en: They live a prosperous, successful life, while Your children suffer as if heavenly wrath had come upon them!

12.24.41.en: Who can comprehend Your wisdom, O Wise and Almighty One?

12.24.42.en: * Behold, all nature preaches to me:

12.24.43.en: Submit to your heavenly Father, who loves you and cares for you.

12.24.44.en: In His hands is all your life; for your sake He brought us into being, and behold, He is preparing a place for you in His divine bosom.

12.24.45.en: Do not rely on your personal experiences alone; your Creator alone gives you wisdom, and reveals to you the understanding of His mysteries.

12.24.46.en: Submit, for by your humility you are raised to the heights.

12.24.47.en: Do not resist and do not contend; does the clay resist its Creator?

12.24.48.en: Who gave you the mouth to speak, the ear to hear, and the hand to touch?

12.24.49.en: Who gave you mind, thought, wisdom and understanding?

12.24.50.en: He loves you; your life and all your gifts are His gifts to you!

12.24.51.en: * My God, who is there to support me but You?

12.24.52.en: Kings, emperors and rulers exalted themselves, and were filled with shame!

12.24.53.en: Strong nations and peoples exalted themselves, and fell before weak nations.

12.24.54.en: My God, grant me the spirit of discernment, that I may walk as Your son!

12.24.55.en: Glory to You, who loved me before I came into being.

12.24.56.en: You shatter my ignorance and folly, and grant me the wisdom that is with You!

12.24.57.en: You dispel my darkness, and grant me Your surpassing light!

12.24.58.en: You put my death to death, and grant me Your glorious resurrection!

12.24.59.en: You expose the devil and his hosts, and cast them under my feet!

12.24.60.en: You give me Yourself, so that I lack nothing!
